work_item.title: Dark/Light Theme Implementation
work_item.description: 🚩 AC Addressed (Required) Introduce light/dark theme selection entirely within the existing Python-rendered web UI. Ensure query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible under both themes. Persist the user’s theme choice across requests using local storage. 💡 What do you want to accomplish? (Required) Improve user experience by allow users to toggle between dark/light themes. 📋 Testability Considerations (Required) Unit tests to check the new dark/light theme functionality.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via a UI control.
The query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible and visually appropriate under both themes.
The selected theme persists across page reloads and new requests by reading from local storage.
Unit tests cover the theme toggle logic and persistence mechanism.

analysis.summary: Implement a user-selectable dark/light theme toggle in the existing Python-rendered web UI, ensuring UI elements including query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible, with user preference persisted via local storage.
technical_requirements: Add a theme toggle control in the web UI to switch between dark and light themes.
Implement CSS styles for both dark and light themes affecting the entire UI, including query syntax highlighting and result panels.
Persist the user's theme choice across page requests using browser local storage.
Ensure the Python-rendered UI templates support dynamic theme application.
Write unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence.
acceptance_criteria: Users can toggle between dark and light themes via a UI control.
The query syntax highlighting and result panels remain legible and visually appropriate under both themes.
The selected theme persists across page reloads and new requests by reading from local storage.
Unit tests cover the theme toggle logic and persistence mechanism.
risks: Ensuring consistent and accessible styling across all UI components under both themes.
Maintaining readability of syntax highlighting and result panels in both themes.
Integration of theme persistence with existing Python-rendered templates without framework support.
Cross-browser compatibility of local storage usage.
analysis.recommended_approach: Define CSS variables or separate style sheets for dark and light themes. Add a JavaScript module to handle theme toggling and persistence using local storage. Modify Python-rendered templates to include theme-related classes or attributes dynamically. Implement unit tests for the JavaScript theme toggle logic and any Python code changes related to theme application.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme CSS styles and update styles.py to include CSS variables for light and dark themes

instructions: Define CSS variables for the light theme: --bg-color: #f8f9fa, --text-color: #333333, --primary-color: #0066cc, --syntax-keyword: #00008b, --syntax-string: #a31515, --result-bg: #ffffff, --result-text: #000000.

Define CSS variables for the dark theme: --bg-color: #1a1a1a, --text-color: #e0e0e0, --primary-color: #4da6ff, --syntax-keyword: #9cdcfe, --syntax-string: #ce9178, --result-bg: #2d2d2d, --result-text: #d4d4d4.
Wrap existing body and UI element styles to use these CSS variables, e.g., body { background-color: var(--bg-color); color: var(--text-color); }.
Add a .dark-theme CSS class that overrides the CSS variables with the dark theme values.
Update syntax highlighting styles and result panel styles to use the CSS variables so they adapt automatically to the theme.
Ensure all UI components that display query syntax and results use these variables for colors to maintain legibility.

implementation_steps.validation: CSS in styles.py contains both light and dark theme variables, existing styles use these variables, and .dark-theme class overrides variables correctly.

implementation_steps.description: Add theme toggle button in the UI and implement JavaScript to handle theme switching and persistence

instructions: Locate the base HTML template rendering function or string where the header or navigation bar is defined.
Insert a button element with id='theme-toggle' and class='theme-toggle-btn' in the header area: <button id='theme-toggle' class='theme-toggle-btn'>🌙 Dark Mode</button>.

Add CSS styles for .theme-toggle-btn in the styles section (if styles.py is referenced here, ensure styles are included or inline styles are added) to style the button with padding, border, cursor pointer, and color consistent with theme variables.
Before the closing </body> tag, add inline JavaScript that performs the following:
- On page load, read the 'theme' value from localStorage.

- If the stored theme is 'dark', add the 'dark-theme' class to the <body> element and update the button text to '☀️ Light Mode'. Otherwise, ensure 'dark-theme' is not present and button text is '🌙 Dark Mode'.
- Add an event listener to the button to toggle the 'dark-theme' class on <body> when clicked.
- Update localStorage with the new theme value ('dark' or 'light').
- Update the button text accordingly after toggle.
Ensure the JavaScript is vanilla and does not rely on external libraries.

implementation_steps.validation: HTML template includes the theme toggle button and JavaScript that reads/writes theme preference to localStorage and toggles the 'dark-theme' class on the body.

implementation_steps.description: Create unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence

instructions: Write unit tests for the JavaScript theme toggle logic using a Python test framework that supports JS testing or mock the JS environment if possible.
Alternatively, write Python tests to verify that the HTML template includes the theme toggle button and the inline JavaScript snippet.
Test that the CSS variables for themes are present in styles.py.
If possible, add integration tests that simulate rendering the template and check for presence of theme toggle elements and scripts.
Include tests to verify that the theme toggle button text changes correctly based on theme state.

implementation_steps.validation: Unit tests exist that verify the presence and correctness of theme toggle UI elements, JavaScript logic, and CSS variables.

implementation.pr_description: Implemented dark/light theme toggle feature with CSS variables in styles.py, added a toggle button and JavaScript for theme switching and persistence in html_template.py, and created unit tests to verify theme toggle functionality and persistence.
